title: A Pod in CrashLoopBackOff
summary: Find out why a Pod keeps restarting, from the first symptom to the fix.

steps.say: Start with the symptom. The Pod restarts again and again, and READY stays at 0/1.
Describe shows the last exit code. Code 1 means the app itself failed, not the platform.

out: Error: environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set
steps.say: Read the logs of the previous run. The container died on a missing setting.
Give the Deployment the missing variable. This starts a new rollout.
The new Pod is Ready. In real life, put the value in a ConfigMap or Secret, not in the command.

takeaway: Describe, then logs --previous, then fix the cause. The exit code tells you whether to blame the app or the platform.

title: A Service with no endpoints
summary: Traffic fails although every Pod is Running. The label selector is the usual cause.

steps.say: The request cannot connect at all, yet the Pods look healthy.
An empty endpoints list means the Service selects no Pods. That is the whole problem.
Read what the Service is looking for.
The Pods are labelled app=shop, but the Service wants app=shop-web.
Fix the selector so it matches the Pod labels.
Endpoints appear at once, and traffic flows.

takeaway: Running Pods do not mean reachable Pods. Check endpoints first when a Service fails.

title: Find what filled the disk
summary: Narrow a full filesystem down to the one directory that caused it.

out: Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
steps.say: The root filesystem is completely full, so writes fail.
Stay on one filesystem with -x and sort. /var holds almost everything.
Go one level deeper. Logs are the culprit.
One debug log grew to 28 GB.
Truncate instead of deleting a file a process still holds open, or the space is not freed.
Space is back. Fix the cause with log rotation or a lower log level.

takeaway: Use du with -x and sort to walk down to the biggest directory. Truncate open files; do not just delete them.

title: Port already in use
summary: A service refuses to start because another process owns its port.

steps.say: The service will not start.

out: !bind() to 0.0.0.0:8080 failed (98: Address already in use)
steps.say: The log names the problem exactly: port 8080 is taken.
ss shows which process listens on the port, and its PID.
It is a forgotten test server, running for three days.

steps.cmd: sudo kill 2211 && sudo systemctl start web
steps.say: Stop the stray process, then start the real service.
The service is up.

takeaway: Read the error, find the owner with ss -ltnp, decide whether to stop it or move your service.

title: SSH refuses the key
summary: A private key with open permissions is ignored. Fix the mode and connect.

steps.say: SSH refuses a key that others can read.
The file is readable by everyone: mode 644.
Only the owner should read and write a private key.
The connection works.

takeaway: A private key must be mode 600. The warning text tells you exactly that.

title: Trace a DNS problem with dig
summary: Tell a bad record from a bad resolver by asking different servers.

steps.say: The default resolver returns nothing for the name.
A public resolver knows the name. So the record exists and our resolver is the problem.
Following the chain from the root confirms the record is published.
The machine uses an internal resolver at 10.0.0.2.
That resolver fails. It needs attention, not the DNS zone.

takeaway: Query the same name from two resolvers. If one answers and one fails, the fault is the resolver.

title: Check a certificate before it expires
summary: Read the dates of a live certificate from the command line.

steps.cmd: echo | openssl s_client -connect shop.example.com:443 -servername shop.example.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
steps.say: The certificate ends in three days.
Compare with today. Three days is too tight to ignore.

steps.cmd: echo | openssl s_client -connect shop.example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer
steps.say: The issuer is an automated CA, so renewal should have happened by itself.

out: !Failed to renew: Timeout during connect (likely firewall problem)
steps.say: Renewal fails because the challenge port is blocked. That is why the certificate is old.

steps.cmd: sudo ufw allow 80/tcp && sudo certbot renew
steps.say: Open the port and renew. Then add monitoring for days left.

takeaway: Certificates fail quietly. Alert on days left, and test renewal, not only issuance.

title: Debug a container that exits
summary: Read the logs, then run a shell in the same image to look around.

steps.say: The container started and stopped within seconds.
The entry file is not where the image expects it.
Override the entrypoint to explore the image.
The build output is in dist, not in /app.

steps.cmd: docker run -d --name api myorg/api:1.4 node dist/server.js
steps.say: Run with the right path. Then fix the Dockerfile CMD.
The container stays up.

takeaway: Logs first, then a shell in the same image. Most start-up failures are wrong paths or missing settings.

title: Terraform plan shows drift
summary: Someone changed a resource by hand. Plan shows what Terraform would undo.

out: Plan: 0 to add, !1 to change, 0 to destroy.
steps.say: Plan shows a change nobody wrote in code. The live rule differs from the configuration.
The live security group is open to the whole internet.

out: a91c2de Restrict web ingress to the VPC
steps.say: The code already says the VPC range. A person edited the console.
Apply puts the rule back as the code says. Then remove console write access.

takeaway: Drift is a signal. Decide whether the code or the console is right, then make them match.

title: Ceph shows HEALTH_WARN: an OSD is down
summary: Read the cluster state, find the down OSD and watch recovery.

steps.say: The cluster is serving data, but one OSD is down and objects have fewer copies.

out: ID  CLASS  WEIGHT   TYPE NAME        STATUS
steps.say: osd.7 on node-c is the one.

steps.cmd: ssh node-c sudo systemctl status ceph-osd@7 | head -3
steps.say: The daemon crashed on that host.

out: bluestore: error reading from device: Input/output error
steps.say: A disk error. Replace the disk, do not just restart.
Mark it out so Ceph rebuilds the copies elsewhere.
Recovery is running. Wait for active+clean before touching anything else.

takeaway: Down is not lost. Check the host and disk, mark it out, and let recovery finish before more changes.

title: Unseal a sealed Vault
summary: After a restart Vault is sealed and serves nothing until enough key shares are entered.

steps.say: Vault is up but sealed. It needs 3 of the 5 key shares.
Each holder enters a share. One share alone does nothing.
The second share.
The third share unseals Vault. It is active again.
Check who you are and how long the token lives. Long-lived tokens are a risk.

takeaway: Unseal needs a quorum of key holders by design. Auto-unseal removes the manual step but not the need to protect the keys.

title: A VM that will not start on Kubernetes
summary: A VirtualMachineInstance stays Scheduling. The cause is usually storage or resources.

steps.say: The VM instance never gets a node.
No node offers the KVM device. Hardware virtualization is missing or the device plugin is not ready.
No node advertises KVM.
Emulation is off, which is right for production. So the nodes need virtualization turned on.
The CPU flags are missing. In a cloud VM, enable nested virtualization or use bare metal.

takeaway: KubeVirt needs real virtualization on the node. Read the scheduling event before changing the VM spec.

title: Latency rose after a deploy
summary: Find a latency shift, date it, link it to a change and roll it back, the way a change correlator would.

steps.cmd: promtool query instant http://prometheus:9090 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="checkout"}[5m])))'
steps.say: The fleet p99 for checkout is 1.82 seconds. A merged histogram gives the correct percentile for the whole service.

steps.cmd: promtool query instant http://prometheus:9090 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="checkout"}[5m] offset 1h)))'
steps.say: One hour earlier the p99 was 0.31 seconds. This is a lasting shift, not a short spike, so something changed.
Ask what changed. A deploy landed at 14:01, a couple of minutes before the shift began. That is a strong suspect by time and by scope.

out: 14:01  Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  Scaled up replica set checkout-7c9 to 6
14:02  Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  Scaled down replica set checkout-5f1 to 0
steps.say: The events confirm the rollout finished at 14:02. No other change touched checkout in the last half hour.
Roll back to the previous revision. This is a moderate-risk action that a person approves after seeing the evidence.

steps.cmd: promtool query instant http://prometheus:9090 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="checkout"}[5m])))'
steps.say: Verify the symptom with the same query that showed the problem. The p99 is back near normal, so the fix worked.
